body.heading: Your voice is a safety tool
paragraphs: You already have one of the best safety tools there is: your voice. These sentences are for moments when something feels wrong — with anyone, anywhere. Using them is never rude, never wrong, and never something you will be in trouble for.
Practice saying them out loud now, while everything is calm. Words you have practiced are words you can find when you need them.

body.heading: Words that stop things
paragraphs: No! — I don't want to do that. You can say no to hugs, games, secrets and dares — even to grown-ups, even to people you know.
Stop! — I don't like this. A clear, loud stop is always allowed.
Don't touch me. — My body belongs to me. Nobody may touch you in ways you don't like or that feel confusing.
Stay away from me. — I don't feel comfortable. You may move away from anyone, any time.

body.heading: Words that get help
paragraphs: I need help. — Please help me. Say it to a trusted adult, a teacher, a shop worker, another parent with children.
I don't know you. — I shouldn't go with people I don't know, even if they know my name or say my parents sent them. (Families can use a secret password instead — ask yours what it is.)
I won't go with you. — I am not coming with you. Then move toward people and help.
That's not okay. — I don't like what you are doing. You may name behavior that feels wrong.
I feel uncomfortable. — Something doesn't feel right. You never need a better reason than that feeling.
I need to tell my parents. — I will speak to someone I trust. Telling is never tattling when it is about safety — and you can keep telling until someone listens and helps.

body.heading: For the grown-ups reading along
paragraphs: Children use these words best when adults have rehearsed them at home without fear or drama: short, calm practice, repeated a few times a year. Agree on a family password for the rare 'someone else must fetch you' situation, remind children that safe adults never ask kids to keep secrets from their parents, and tell them often: you will always believe them, and they will never be in trouble for telling.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Which three of these sentences feel most important for YOU to practice? Say each one out loud twice — once quietly, once in your strong voice.
2. Who are three trusted adults you could say 'I need help' to — one at home, one at school, one in your neighborhood?

takeaway: No, stop, don't touch me, I need help, I need to tell my parents — practiced safety words, used without fear, backed by trusted adults who always listen.
materials: Just you and this page — plus a calm conversation with a trusted grown-up
supervision: Read this one together with a trusted grown-up. It is written to be rehearsed out loud, calmly, more than once.
safetyNotes: This page teaches safety words only — no activities, no meeting anyone, nothing to try out with strangers.
Grown-ups: agree on a family password, name the child's trusted adults together, and make clear the child will never be in trouble for telling.
If a child discloses something worrying while reading this page, believe them, stay calm, and contact local child-protection services or police.
screenFreeExtension: Practice the strong sentences out loud together on a walk — calm voices first, then playground voices — and name your family's three trusted adults.
